guided.eyebrow: NIS2 software for companies with 50 to 150 employees
guided.title: Been asked to handle <blue>NIS2</blue>?
guided.subtitle: In the end you have everything in one document: what is done, what is still open, and your management's approval with name and date. The app writes the texts.
guided.trainingCta: Free training for your Managing Director

meta.title: NIS2 software: step by step, for companies with 50 to 150 employees
meta.description: You fill it in, we explain every point in plain words, and at the end management signs. For companies without their own security department.

walk.heroAlt: The NIS2 walkthrough: your path step by step, the first items done
walk.title: How you get there
walk.lead: Like tax software: you enter what only your company knows, its software, suppliers and risks. The app writes the texts, and management approves them. Every picture shows the real app, filled in for made-up example companies.

oneAtATime.title: One thing at a time
oneAtATime.text: You only ever see one item. We explain it in plain words before you enter anything, and the law behind it is one click away.
oneAtATime.alt: A step in the walkthrough: registering with your authority, explained in plain words

bsiMethods.title: Methods from the BSI
bsiMethods.text: Where Germany's Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) recommends a method, it is ready for you, such as the risk assessment from BSI Standard 200-3. One click makes it your company's method. Whether you adopt it is your decision.
bsiMethods.alt: The risk assessment method from BSI Standard 200-3, as an entry in the records

riskMap.title: Your risks at a glance
riskMap.text: You rate your software, your technology and your suppliers on the BSI's matrix. The overview shows where your entries sit and what needs protection first.
riskMap.alt: An example company's risk matrix: how many entries sit in each field

setAside.title: Leaving things open is fine
setAside.text: What cannot be done yet, you set aside with a reason, for example because you are waiting for a letter or need to ask someone first. The item goes on your waiting list and you carry on with the next one.
setAside.alt: Setting an item aside: the reasons to choose from

signOff.title: Management approves in the app
signOff.text: At the end, management reads the documents the app wrote and approves them, signed in with its own account. Its name and the date then appear on each document. Nothing is printed or scanned.
signOff.alt: The walkthrough's documents, approved by management, each with name and date

staysCurrent.title: Stays current
staysCurrent.text: After the approval, one page shows what stays with you: what to do when something happens, and what comes round again. When a date comes due or you change a list, the item goes back to management for approval.
staysCurrent.alt: What stays after the approval: what to do when something happens and what recurs, each with its legal basis

outcomes.title: What you hold at the end

registers.title: Your registers
registers.text: What you tick and enter step by step is then in your registers: assets, suppliers, risks, policies, trainings and management reviews.
registers.alt: The asset list in the walkthrough: business processes to tick

log.title: The activity log
log.text: It shows, day by day, who changed what and when. Every approval by management is in it too.

export.title: Everything in one document
export.text: Everything from start to finish: status, open points, documents, risk matrix, every register and answer. Save it as a PDF from the browser.

topic.title: Where this comes up in the walkthrough
topic.lead: The walkthrough turns this into steps you fill in, with the law explained beside each one. Open a step to see its screen, filled in for a made-up company.

national.title: What the national law changes, and what it doesn't
national.lead: The national law decides, among other things, where you register and whom you report incidents to. The measures themselves start from the same minimum list in every member state (Art. 21 NIS 2). The walkthrough takes you through them one step at a time:

landing.title: Halve Europe's <blue>NIS2</blue> bill.
landing.subtitle: The free platform for regulated companies and their suppliers to implement NIS2: self-assessment, templates, and management training. <os>Open source</os>, no lock-in.
landing.productLine: Free NIS2 compliance and information for regulated companies and their suppliers.
landing.supplierDoor: Received a NIS2 questionnaire from a customer? Go to the supplier portal.
landing.trust3: Built to the strictest standard (BSIG §30, IT-Grundschutz), valid across the EU
landing.cardOpenSource: The platform is open source and free to host yourself. We earn from the guided walkthrough, not from your data. The code and schemas are open on GitHub, so you can check for yourself. Everything exportable, no lock-in.
landing.badgeTooltip: The German BSIG (BSI-Gesetz) transposing the EU NIS2 Directive requires affected entities to implement all cybersecurity measures by March 2026. Non-compliance carries fines up to €10M or 2% of global turnover, and personal liability for managing directors.
landing.nis2BadgeTooltip: Built on the full NIS2 Directive covering all 27 EU member states. All 10 Article 21 cybersecurity measures mapped and implemented. Valid across every EU country, not just Germany.
landing.cirBadgeTooltip: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 defines the strictest technical requirements for NIS2 compliance. It establishes the common baseline across all EU member states for DNS providers, TLD registries, cloud providers, data centres, CDNs, managed services, managed security services, online marketplaces, search engines, social networks, and trust service providers.
landing.bsigBadgeTooltip: Built on the German BSIG §30 -- the strictest NIS2 transposition in the EU -- with IT-Grundschutz methodology defaults. Comply once, valid across 27 EU member states. §44(2) BSIG recognises Grundschutz implementation as NIS2 compliance.
